title: Writing for Others
text:
The best investment you can make is in yourself, but the only check you can cash comes from helping others.
Crafting ideas into something helpful to others, or even just plain entertaining? That’s good for everyone.
The moment you compromise that premise by using AI with the intention of “fooling” others into thinking the post is somehow more valuable than it is?
The only person you’re fooling is yourself.

Am I arguing against using AI for editing? No. 
Idea generation? No.
Preliminary research? No.

What I’m arguing against is the intention: you’re trying to make a buck off people’s inability to discern real from fake when talking about what you believe and why.
You’re no longer focused on adding value, you’re focused on the appearance of value.
The public-facing signal in this transgression is doubly negative. It says: “I’m a commodity with premium pricing, and I think YOU can’t tell the difference.”
All I can say is be careful of labelling people as luddites when they disagree with using AI. It says more about you than it does about them.

title: Why Write in The Age of AI?
text:
Every extra word feels like defiance when a little voice in my head whispers:

“What’s the point of writing if AI can just do it faster and easier?”

If LLMs are trained on the weighted popularity of our ideas, then the most subversive thing to do is charge, screaming wildly, into LLM’s bottomless appetite for training data.
You want representation in the collective consciousness of LLM models?
Then you gotta vote with your voice- don’t go quietly into the dark-night of economic nihilism and existential despair1.

title: Why Write in The Age of AI?
section: 0.2 That’s something an AI shill would say!
text:
0.2 That’s something an AI shill would say!
Okay keyboard warrior, this is why you’re wrong- a strong democratic republic is vital and (for better or worse) there’s one political party advocating for it and it starts with the letter “D”.
So when the Stanford Business School starts tracking the consistent left-leaning slant of large langauge models that’s us winning.
So those margins? The one’s where it says “+D”? They’re small, humble, little margins but they’re there and they’re consistent for all the models listed.
In fact, it’s true for all the models.
So when there’s a machine answering stupid people’s questions at scale which they take without a gram of critical reflection2, you bet your ass that it’s in your best interest to write from the soul and try and compete in the marketplace of ideas.
